versions.prompt:
Stylized hand-painted 3D game environment art for a fast first-person roguelite shooter, matching the
readable visual direction of Gunfire Reborn: bold chunky silhouettes, broad clean faceted planes, two or three dominant
colour blocks, soft painted gradients and a few restrained edge accents. East-Asian underground forge-palace fantasy of Zhurong, the Chinese god of fire: massive black iron (xuan tie) with heavy rivets, dark charcoal basalt blocks, deep vermilion lacquer, warm aged bronze ding cauldrons, chunky thick iron chains always attached flat to the surfaces, soot-darkened edges, and a few channels and cracks of molten lava. Lava, embers and fire are painted as opaque flat bright orange-yellow surfaces, never as smoke, loose sparks or transparent effects. Matte stone,
wood and cloth, restrained highlights on metal, sparse painted wear. No photorealism, micro-grain, dense tiny cracks,
elaborate miniature carvings, harsh specular highlights or baked cast shadows. Even neutral lighting.

Asset (18m wide x 5m tall x 8m deep): A colossal forge bellows lying on the floor of a blast hall, 18m long, 5m tall and 8m deep: a huge accordion bag of thick dark oxblood-red leather with big rounded pleats running across its length, stretched between a heavy flat black iron top board and a black iron base frame on squat beast-paw feet; at the RIGHT end it narrows into a massive cast bronze nozzle shaped like a roaring beast head that points into the furnace; a thick black iron pumping beam with a chain lies along the top board; rows of big rivets, soot on the edges, a faint orange glow inside the beast's mouth painted as an opaque bright orange-yellow surface. PROPORTIONS: the FRONT and BACK views are drawn about 3.6 times as wide as tall, a long low machine; the LEFT and RIGHT views about 1.6 times as wide as tall. Chunky readable forms, no smoke, no fire. One solid connected piece on a flat base.

Output: one orthographic model turnaround sheet for 3D reconstruction. Exactly four separate complete views
of the SAME object in one row, left to right:
1. FRONT view: the object's front faces the viewer.
2. LEFT side view: the object turned 90 degrees so its front points to the LEFT edge of the image (camera at the
   object's right-hand side).
3. BACK view: the object's back faces the viewer.
4. RIGHT side view: the object turned 90 degrees so its front points to the RIGHT edge of the image.
Same scale and same ground line in all four, each centred in its quarter with generous empty margin, never touching or
overlapping; the whole object fits inside its quarter, nothing cropped.
Plain flat light neutral grey background (#D6D6D6). No floor, no ground shadow, no text, no labels, no frames, no
perspective.
